alternatives.whyRejected: Trivially edited, and it exposes record numbering.
Needs key management and rotation and adds per-key cost. Authorization belongs in the application, not in the identifier.

fields.consequences: Accidental corruption and casual tampering are detected, and external keys stay short and URL-safe. They are not cryptographically secure: anyone can decode or forge one, so applications must still authorize every access. The format is part of the public contract, so changing it breaks stored and bookmarked keys.
fields.context: Sharded record identities must cross the application boundary as one opaque, URL-safe value in REST routes, links and JSON. Plain concatenations such as `3-1042` invite casual editing, and a mistyped or truncated value should fail loudly rather than address a different record.
fields.decision: A ShardKey's external string is its binary form bit-inverted, suffixed with a 2-byte Fletcher checksum, and encoded in a URL-safe Modified Base64 alphabet. Parsing rejects a string whose checksum or type metadata does not match. No cryptographic key material is involved.
fields.title: External keys are obfuscated and checksummed, not encrypted or signed
